batch_rationale: The controlled nitroacetophenone rows separate solvent-ratio response from loading response over part of the series. The remaining rows cover acids, alcohols, amines, esters, nitriles, ethers, ketones and non-H-bonding controls across strong and weak eluents. Where loading amount or carrier volume changes, those comparisons are explicitly treated as confounded. The batch is intended to improve prediction across the row distribution after retraining, not to maximize retention.
batch_strategy: Use diverse structural and condition references alongside a controlled nitroacetophenone solvent-ratio sequence and fixed-solvent loading contrast. Treat high predicted volumes and q10-q90 spans as reasons to inspect model behavior, not as measured outcomes or calibrated uncertainty.

choices.reason: Fluorinated aromatic ester at 2/1 and relatively high loading; adds a moderate-polarity reference away from the weak-eluent edge.
Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde at 5/1 probes two strongly polar substituents and provides a structural comparison for the nitroacetophenone series.
Cyclohexyl phenyl ketone at 10/1 tests a relatively hydrophobic ketone under weak eluent.
Thioether-substituted acetophenone at 1/1 tests whether sulfur substitution changes behavior beyond the ketone scaffold.
Methoxy aromatic ester at 20/1 extends the measured 10/1 example to weaker eluent; loading also changes, so this is not an isolated solvent contrast.
Methylbenzaldehyde at 5/1 with PE loading solvent supplies a common carbonyl reference under a less represented loading-carrier condition.
Non-H-bonding alkenylbenzene at 5/1 provides a low-polarity control against the many carbonyl-containing selections.
Novel hydroxy-methoxy benzaldehyde at 20/1 tests donor and acceptor interactions under weak eluent; interpretation must retain its high loading and DCM carrier volume.
Cinnamic acid probes an acidic donor at 5/1. Its 1500 uL DCM loading-solvent volume makes it a distinct condition, not a clean acid-versus-neutral comparison.
Dibenzoylmethane at 2/1 tests a two-carbonyl, potentially enolizing structure at low loading.
Novel anisole at 5/1 supplies a simple ether reference for separating aromatic substitution from stronger carbonyl interactions.
Brominated dimethoxybenzene at 50/1 extends the measured pure-EA structure to the weak-eluent edge; loading also differs.
Rigid fused-ring ketone at 10/1 tests whether aromatic shape and carbonyl accessibility differ from simpler aryl ketones.
Dimethylbenzonitrile at 5/1 adds a nitrile-only aromatic reference against the ketone and aldehyde examples.
Bromoanisole at 1/1 anchors a weakly accepting aromatic ether in relatively strong eluent.
Amino benzoate at 10/1 probes an amine donor alongside an ester acceptor, with PE rather than DCM loading solvent.
Brominated aliphatic acid at 5/1 complements the aromatic acid while testing halogen and acid interactions.
Phenylalkyl alcohol at 5/1 tests a single alcohol donor without a carbonyl, using PE loading solvent.
Bulky brominated triaryl hydrocarbon supplies a high-LogP, no-donor/no-acceptor reference; its 600 uL DCM carrier volume is retained as a condition difference.
Novel ring-expanded aromatic ketone at 10/1 tests transfer from measured aromatic ketones to a different fused-ring geometry.
Novel nitroacetophenone at 10/1 tests the weak-eluent region for a ketone bearing a strongly accepting nitro group.
Novel diethyl malonate at 50/1 adds an aliphatic diester at the weak-eluent edge, distinct from aromatic esters.
Benzoyl benzonitrile at 10/1 tests combined nitrile and ketone interactions against the nitrile-only and ketone-only references.
Low-similarity aliphatic ketonitrile at 1/1 broadens structural coverage beyond the predominantly aromatic examples.
Low-similarity halogenated arene at 20/1 is a non-H-bonding control for interpreting polar compounds under weak eluent.
Nitroacetophenone at 1/1 and 67.25 mg starts a fixed-solvent loading contrast; the predictor gives nearly the same volumes across its loading levels.
Nitroacetophenone in pure EA at 134.5 mg begins a same-molecule, same-loading solvent-ratio sequence.
Nitroacetophenone at 2/1 and 134.5 mg extends the controlled solvent-ratio sequence from pure EA through 1/1.
Nitroacetophenone at 1/1 and 201.75 mg completes a three-level loading contrast with unchanged eluent and loading carrier.
Nitroacetophenone at 1/1 and 134.5 mg is the shared control for the solvent-ratio sequence and fixed-solvent loading contrast.
Nitroacetophenone at 10/1 probes the predicted high-retention end of its condition series; loading differs from the controlled low-PE-fraction sequence.
Nitroacetophenone at 5/1 fills the intermediate weak-eluent region, while its lower loading prevents treating the full series as a pure solvent contrast.

belief.next_discriminating_question: How do measured V1, V2 and interval width change across the three fixed-condition loading levels?
belief.statement: For nitroacetophenone at fixed 1/1 eluent and loading-carrier conditions, measured loading effects on V1 or V2 may exceed the predictor's nearly flat response across 67.25 to 201.75 mg.
belief.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A measured departure would identify a condition-response failure relevant beyond this molecule; agreement would discourage spending later batches on similar loading contrasts.

hypothesis_updates.reason: Three viewed nitroacetophenone rows hold solvent and loading carrier fixed while varying loading; predictions change very little.

belief.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 134.5 mg loading and identical carrier conditions, how do nitroacetophenone V1 and V2 change from pure EA to 1/1 and 2/1?
belief.statement: Increasing the PE fraction often increases retention on normal-phase silica, but the magnitude and even the observed trend can depend on structure and conditions.
belief.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A controlled solvent-ratio curve can reveal where the predictor transfers solvent effects poorly without imposing a universal monotonic rule.

hypothesis_updates.reason: The controlled portion of the nitroacetophenone series can test the normal-phase solvent-strength prior; other extensions cover weaker eluents but change loading.

open_scientific_questions: Does measured nitroacetophenone loading dependence differ from the predictor's nearly invariant response at fixed 1/1 conditions?
How reliably does the model transfer solvent-ratio response from the controlled nitroacetophenone sequence to other polar structures?
Do acidic and H-bond-donating structures show systematic errors distinct from neutral acceptors under weak eluent?
Which apparent condition effects remain after accounting for loading amount and loading-solvent volume?
